title: Delivery photos over a poor network
summary: Get proof-of-delivery photos from riders' phones to the server, whatever the network does.
context: Cubbon Couriers' riders take a photo at each door, up to 80 a day. The photos settle disputes, so a lost one may cost a refund. Riders often work in basements and on cheap phones with little free space, and they will not wait for an upload to finish.
Stored photos have become the largest part of the bill. Almost nobody looks at a photo after a fortnight, but disputes may arrive for up to 90 days.
must_handle: The rider moves on immediately, and the upload happens later by itself.
No photo is lost if the app is closed or the phone restarts.
Photos use little data and little space on the phone.
A photo cannot be swapped or faked easily.
Storage gets cheaper as photos age, and they are deleted on a schedule.
show_in_answer: The life of a photo, from camera to deletion.
How uploads are queued, retried and resumed.
Where the image goes and who can read it.
A rough storage estimate, with what would bring it down.
